 'GO' evacuation orders, road closures across Valley due to flash flooding
 Prev 
 Next 
 Viewer videos show flooding on Interstate 17 near Munds Park on Sunday morning. 
 By: 
 abc15.com staff 
 Posted 
 and last updated 
 Share Copy link Facebook Nextdoor X Threads Reddit LinkedIn Email WhatsApp Messenger Print 
 Add ABC15 as a Google Preferred Source 
 (KNXV) — Evacuation orders and road closures were in effect Sunday for multiple areas of the region due to flash flooding.
 ROAD CLOSURES : 
 Just before 3 p.m., the Arizona Department of Transportation announced all Interstate 17 lanes that were impacted by today's flooding were reopened.
 ADOT officials say the following highways remained closed as of 3:30 p.m.:
 State Route 89A between Sedona and Kachina Village (mileposts 375-397)
 State Route 73 between Indian Pine and White River (mileposts 357-351)
 State Route 238 between Maricopa and Gila Bend
 ADOT officials said, "Crews are responding to rockfall across northern Arizona, using plow trucks to clear roadways, making travel safer for motorists."
 In Flagstaff, motorists are being warned of the following flood-related road closures:
 S Milton Road
 Route 66
 Butler Avenue
 E Huntington Drive
 S Lone Tree Road
 COUNTY EMERGENCIES : 
 On Sunday, Coconino County officials activated the Emergency Operations Center as flooding hits the region.
 With the activation of the EOC, a call center (phone number 928-679-8525) is in place with updated information on evacuations, road closures and sandbags.
 County officials say sandbags can be obtained at Pinewood Fire Department (475 E. Pinewood Blvd.) and Highlands Fire Department (3350 Old Munds Hwy.).
 Additionally, residents can fill their own sandbags at Thorpe Park (parking lot at north end of N. Aztec St., between Frances Short Pond and softball fields). Residents are advised to bring their own shovels.
 As a regional Flood Watch continues, county updates can be found at coconino.az.gov/ready .
 The EOC activation comes two days after Gov. Hobbs declared a state of emergency for both Coconino and Navajo counties .
 EVACUATION ORDERS : 
 City of Sedona officials said Evacuation Zones 8, 9, and 10 are in a “GO STATUS,” which means anyone in those areas must leave immediately.
 An evacuation center was set up at Sedona Red Rock High School (995 Upper Red Rock Loop Rd.).
 City officials added Oak Creek is “rising quickly,” reminding citizens to avoid creek beds and washes, and to not cross rushing water that is on the road.
 Complete information on Sedona evacuation orders can be found at https://www.sedonaaz.gov/your-government/departments/police/emergency-management .
 City of Sedona 
 Evacuation map (Nov. 1, 2026) 
 Cedar Creek residents along the river were also under a “GO” evacuation order Sunday morning, with Canyon Day Junior High established as an evacuation center.
 The White Mountain Tribe EOC said in a social media post: “Residents along River Rd. are now placed on "Set" status. Please prepare to leave your homes quickly if water levels continue to rise. Pack medication, clothes, charge your phones, flashlights and other essential items you will need. Know your exit routes and check on elderly and neighbors.”
 Additionally, sheriff's officials said Lone Pine Dam Road at Linden Wash in Linden was shut down because of flooding.
 In Gila County, residents and visitors at Greenback Valley RV Park in Tonto Basin were told to evacuate immediately.
 A evacuation shelter was established at Tonto Basin Elementary School (445 S. Old Hwy 188).
 The Camp Verde Marshal’s Office notified residents near Verde River, West Clear Creek, and Wet Beaver Creek to immediately evacuate due to flooding.
 A shelter is available for evacuees at Camp Verde Parks and Recreation Gym (473 Main St.).
